findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Uncheck both ACs ([ ]) so they are ticked only after the Windows run ids are recorded in comments.
evidence: "- [x] Every line removed from `crlf.args` names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix"
Testing: "AC1 evidence: the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main whose head contains the merge commit. Its run id goes in a comment before the close."
findings.finding: Both acceptance criteria are already marked done ([x]) even though the plan's own Testing section says the evidence (the Windows validation run id and the first main sweep run id) has not been produced yet.
scenarios: An executor or closing gate reads the ticked boxes as satisfied and closes the ticket without recording the run ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Change both '- [x]' to '- [ ]' in the Acceptance Criteria section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py (both run_git and the _run_in_group/timeout path) and the tier2 no-\r alternates assertion exist and pass under `make verify`.
evidence: Approach: "New regression tests: tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py ... In test_plan_replay_tier2, an assertion that the alternates file contains no `\r`."
Both ACs reference only `crlf.args` lines and `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
findings.finding: The ACs only cover crlf.args bookkeeping. Nothing covers the product-code deliverables: the gitutil str-stdin contract change (run_git and _run_in_group), the tier2 alternates fix, the new tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py, or the tier2 no-\r assertion. Those POSIX-runnable regression guards could be omitted or fail while both ACs still pass, for example if one test is fixed some other way or its line is reclassified as unsupported.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria vs Approach 'New regression tests'
scenarios: The gitutil fix lands without the spy-based tests. A later refactor reintroduces text-mode stdin, and only the Windows sweep (if it runs) catches it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: '- [ ] `tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py` asserts str input reaches subprocess.run and subprocess.Popen as encoded bytes with text false, decoded output, and str-bearing CalledProcessError; `test_plan_replay_tier2` asserts the alternates file has no `\r`; both pass in `make verify`.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default: remove all 11 lines, run Windows validation, and fix-and-rerun any failure. Only a test with a recorded non-fixable Windows reason may be restored to crlf.args, and validation reruns on the final tree.
evidence: Approach: "`.github/windows-sweep-deselect/crlf.args`: remove each line whose test passes in the Windows validation run."
Testing: "Pre-merge Windows validation on the exact fixed tree, with the lines removed"
AC2: "or each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason."
findings.finding: The validation procedure is ambiguous and partly circular. Approach says to remove only lines whose tests pass in the Windows validation run. Testing says that run happens 'with the lines removed' (a test can only pass if its line is removed first). Neither section says what happens to a line whose test still fails, even though every one of the 11 tests has a planned fix. AC2's 'intentionally unsupported' escape hatch could absorb a broken fix.
findings.location: Approach (crlf.args bullet) vs Testing (pre-merge Windows validation) vs AC2
scenarios: The reclaim test still fails because pangolin's stub has not landed on main. The executor must guess whether to re-add the line (which changes the validated tree), block, or mark it unsupported.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the crlf.args bullet with: 'Remove all 11 lines; dispatch the Windows validation on that tree; any failing test is fixed and the run repeated. Restore a line only for a test documented on the ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows (with reason), then re-run validation on the final tree before merge.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Allow AC1 evidence to come from a `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref main` dispatch on the merge commit (or the first scheduled run, whichever comes first).
evidence: "AC1 evidence: the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main whose head contains the merge commit."
findings.finding: AC1's evidence waits for 'the first scheduled test.yml run on main' after merge. That ties completion to the schedule's timing rather than to an action the executor can take in-session. The plan already uses `gh workflow run 294845723` for the pre-merge run and could dispatch the same workflow on main immediately after merge.
scenarios: The merge lands just after the nightly cron, so closure waits a day or more for a run the executor could have dispatched.
findings.suggested_fix: Testing: 'AC1 evidence: a `sweep (windows)` job in a test.yml run on main whose head contains the merge commit — dispatch `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref main` right after merge rather than waiting for the schedule.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Move sub-cause 6 (test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement_does_not_fail_dry_run) out of this CRLF ticket into a child or pangolin follow-up, or add an AC clause allowing a line to remain when it is recorded as blocked on a named ticket.
evidence: "This is not line endings; it is the shell-stub problem transhuman-wounded-pangolin solves with `tests/_exe_stub.py`."
"This waits for pangolin's change on main."
AC: "each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason"
Title: "11 tests fail on CRLF from core.autocrlf=true or text-mode newline translation"
findings.finding: Sub-cause 6 (test_reclaim_bridge_history's sh-stub ref injection) is, by the plan's own words, 'not line endings'. It is blocked on transhuman-wounded-pangolin landing on main, yet it is bundled into the CRLF ticket. AC2 only lets remaining crlf.args lines stand if they are 'intentionally unsupported on Windows'. This test is merely dependency-blocked, not unsupported, so a pangolin delay leaves the 10 independently-ready CRLF fixes unable to close.
findings.location: Root cause §6 / Approach §6 ('This waits for pangolin's change on main') / Acceptance Criteria line 2
scenarios: Pangolin is delayed or reworked. The gitutil/tier2/.gitattributes/test fixes are ready and validated, but the ticket cannot satisfy AC2 because the reclaim test is neither passing nor 'intentionally unsupported'.
Whoever implements this either waits on an external ticket or misrecords a dependency-blocked test as 'intentionally unsupported' to close.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-home the reclaim-test line under a ticket that depends on transhuman-wounded-pangolin (or under pangolin itself). Alternatively, extend AC2 to: 'or each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows, or as blocked on a named open ticket, with the reason'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Put the str-stdin handling in one place, at run_git's entry before the timeout/_run_in_group split, rather than writing it a second time inside `_run_in_group` (its only caller is run_git, gitutil.py:208).
evidence: grep `_run_in_group(` in src/: only gitutil.py:208 (the call inside run_git) and gitutil.py:282 (its definition). There are no other callers.

gitutil.py:207-216: run_git calls `_run_in_group(..., text=text, ..., input=input_data)` only when `timeout is not None`. A str-stdin branch placed before line 206 would therefore cover both the subprocess.run path and the _run_in_group path.
The plan's own regression test already reaches _run_in_group "through `run_git(timeout=...)`", which confirms the entry point is shared.
findings.finding: Approach step 1 says to "Apply the same in `_run_in_group`", which points to a second copy of the encode-stdin / decode-output / deferred-check logic. `_run_in_group` has one caller, run_git (when timeout is set), so handling str input once at run_git's entry, before the timeout branch, already covers that path. Two copies can drift apart, for example in how TimeoutExpired output gets decoded.
scenarios: An implementer adds separate encode/decode/check code to both `run_git` and `_run_in_group`. Later one copy changes its TimeoutExpired decoding or universal-newline handling and the other does not, so the timeout path and the no-timeout path return different str output.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the bullet to: "Handle str `input_data` once in `run_git` before the timeout branch (encode it, re-enter run_git with `text=False, check=False`, then decode stdout/stderr and apply `check`). `_run_in_group` is reached only through run_git, so it is covered without a second copy." Keep the Popen-spied regression test as the evidence that the timeout path is covered.
